- When sentiment turns sharply positive (e.g., +1.00) followed by a spike in news volume, model tends to overreact and overshoot — reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- If sentiment shows strong negative momentum (e.g., -1.00 or -0.67) with high news volume, model underreacts — adjust downward by 3–7% to match true mean reversion.
- Model consistently underestimates true price in periods with high sentiment volatility — apply a +2%–+5% bias correction for volatile sentiment windows.
- In cases of sustained high sentiment + high news volume, model forecasts lag behind true price by 1–3 days — add 1–2% daily momentum adjustment to catch up.
- When sentiment is flat or neutral (0.00–0.33) and news volume is low, model overpredicts — apply -1%–-3% correction to avoid overconfidence bias.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome shows strong upward trend after a dip, model often fails to capture momentum — apply +3%–+5% adjustment to the later half of forecast horizon.
